source_text: Ad reliqua festinat oratio, sed premendus adhuc locus est, ut divisionibus quam possumus brevibus, lectori et intellegentia rei et memoria suggeratur. In omnibus quidem pene rebus homonymorum, quae aequivoca appellamus, conditio reperitur.
pass_a_gloss: The speech hurries to the remaining things, but the place is still to be pressed, so that by divisions as brief as we can the reader may be supplied both with understanding of the matter and with memory. In almost all things indeed the condition of homonyms, which we call equivocals, is found.
pass_b_english: The discussion hurries toward what remains, but we must press this point further, dividing it as briefly as possible to help the reader both understand and remember it. In almost every area we find homonyms, which we call words with more than one meaning.

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at 2.51; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
